title: Can salvation be lost?
paragraphs: Can Salvation Be Lost? A Biblical Study

The question of whether a believer can lose their salvation is one of the most frequently discussed topics in Christian theology. This study will explore what the Bible teaches about the security of salvation, addressing the passages that are commonly cited on both sides of the discussion, and conclude with the mainstream Evangelical understanding.
The Promise of Eternal Security
Several passages in Scripture emphasize the assurance and security believers have in Christ. Jesus Himself spoke of the permanence of salvation for those who are truly His:

And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who hath given them unto me, is greater than all; and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father's hand. - John 10:28-29 ASV
Apostle Paul also speaks of the unbreakable love of God for believers:

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. - Romans 8:38-39 ASV
Paul further assures believers of God’s faithfulness in completing the work He began in them:
being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will perfect it until the day of Jesus Christ: - Philippians 1:6 ASV
Passages Warning Against Falling Away
However, there are also passages that warn believers about falling away. One of the most debated is found in Hebrews:

For as touching those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, and tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come, and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. - Hebrews 6:4-6 ASV
Another warning is found in Jesus’ words:

Every branch in me that beareth not fruit, he taketh it away... If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. - John 15:2, 6 ASV
Understanding the Tension
How do we reconcile these Scriptures? There are several common ways Bible-believing Christians interpret these passages:

Perseverance of the Saints (Eternal Security): The mainstream Evangelical view is that those who are truly born again will persevere in faith until the end. Passages warning against falling away are seen as directed at those who profess faith but were never truly converted (1 John 2:19 ASV).
Warnings as Means: The warnings serve as God’s means to keep believers in the faith, encouraging self-examination and dependence on Christ (2 Corinthians 13:5 ASV).

Conditional Security: Some interpret these warnings to mean that genuine believers can forfeit their salvation by apostasy or persistent unbelief. However, this view is less supported by passages emphasizing God’s sustaining grace.
The Assurance of Salvation
The Bible encourages believers to have assurance of their salvation, not based on personal performance, but on the finished work of Christ and the promises of God:
These things have I written unto you, that ye may know that ye have eternal life, even unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God. - 1 John 5:13 ASV
Salvation is by grace through faith, not by works, and is secured by God’s power:
for by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man should glory. - Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV
who by the power of God are guarded through faith unto a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. - 1 Peter 1:5 ASV
Conclusion

In summary, the weight of biblical evidence supports the view that true believers cannot lose their salvation. The warnings in Scripture serve as a call to genuine faith and perseverance, not as an indication that salvation is easily lost. Those who truly belong to Christ are kept by His power and can rest in His promises.
